newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Moonstone diamond ship docks for repair.
newsitem.headline: Moonstone diamond ship docks for repair.

text.p: Marine diamond hunter Moonstone Diamond Corp NL said on Monday its offshore mining vessel has been dry docked in East London, South Africa, for repairs.
Moonstone said it would take about a week from when the vessel, "Moonstar," was dry docked on August 14 to repair a 20 mm hole in the propulsion area of the ship's hull.
The hole, which was discovered in July, was caused by an improperly attached earth lead earlier in the ship's life, it said.
Moonstone said the vessel was quite safe, although company policy required the ship return to port.
A shortage of dry dock facilities in Cape Town meant the vessel had to sail to East London for repairs, the company said.
The repairs, including sailing time, will take about three weeks in total, with subsequent test work and monitoring taking a further three weeks, Moonstone said.
The vessel is jointly operated by Moonstone and Benguela Concessions Ltd of South Africa.
The joint venture's next diamond sale, scheduled for late August, would proceed as planned, a company spokeswoman said.
An auction last April saw a parcel of diamonds recovered by the Moonstar weighing 2,908.79 carats fetch an average of US$237.64 per carat.
Moonstone has said it hopes to recover up to 65,000 carats a year.
Moonstone shares were trading one-half cent higher at 17.5 cents on the Australian Stock Exchange at 0310 GMT (1.10 p.m.)
